claim: A municipal body assumes an affirmative duty of care toward pedestrians when it has received repeated written notice of a hazardous sidewalk condition and fails to remediate it within a reasonable time. The Ninth Circuit held that the Tucson City Council's eighteen-month inaction following documented complaints brought it within the scope of actionable negligence under Arizona tort principles.
citation: Aberfoyle v. Tucson City Council, 683 F.3d 441 (9th Cir. 2011)
initial_reasoning: Aberfoyle v. Tucson City Council (2011) held that the city did not owe a duty of care to pedestrians because it had no evidence that the council had actual knowledge of the hazardous sidewalk; the court rejected the notion that repeated complaints alone created an affirmative duty. Thus the citation contradicts the claim that the Ninth Circuit found the city liable for inaction.
